svg.title: a freshly generated project passes its own quality gate: DevSkim scans a large project on a developer's machine as in CI, and still skips the project's tmp folder
svg.text: a freshly generated project passes its own quality gate
Scenario: DevSkim scans a large project on a developer's machine as in CI, and still skips the project's tmp

g.text: Given a generated project holds 1500 ordinary source files, an http:// address and a copy in
A project generated from the toolbox holds 1,500 ordinary source files, counted on the first line. src/fetch.js reads
its data from an http:// address, and tmp/scratch.js, a scratch file in the project's own tmp folder, is a copy of it.
Below them, DevSkim's settings: the folders it skips. The tmp entry, **/?*/tmp/**, wants a folder name before tmp: it
matches the project's own tmp folder, never a tmp folder the project sits in.

text.tspan: find src/modules -type f | wc -l; head -n 1 src/fetch.js tmp/scratch.js && cat .config/devskim/config.json

g.text: Then on the developer's machine DevSkim flags the address in the source and skips the copy
The developer runs MegaLinter with DevSkim alone, then reads the findings back from the report that run wrote.
MegaLinter mounts the project under /tmp/lint, a path that starts with tmp.
The finding fails the run, so task ends on "exit code 201". The report holds one finding: DS137138, an insecure URL, in
src/fetch.js, and nothing in tmp/scratch.js. The test also runs task megalinter:ci under /builds with an initial limit
of 1,024 open files: its new report must flag the same source file.

svg.text: Storyboard e2e · 2 steps · 2 frames · every frame is its own pixel baseline (tolerance: 0)
